[];` followed by `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration !== "google_calendar"` without optional chaining. When destinationCalendar is null/empty, destructuring yields undefined and `undefined.integration` throws TypeError, whereas the old code safely returned undefined and triggered the Cal Video fallback. Verified directly in EventManager.ts hunk.

judged_text: The Google Meet fallback check dereferences mainHostDestinationCalendar without optional chaining, so it throws TypeError when evt.destinationCalendar is null or an empty array, whereas the old code used evt.destinationCalendar?.integration and fell through to switching location to Cal Video. Any booking with location set to Google Meet and no destination calendar (the exact scenario this fallback exists for) crashes with 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading integration)' and the booking fails with a 500 instead of falling back to Cal Video.

record.issue_text: [BUG] The Google Meet fallback check dereferences mainHostDestinationCalendar without optional chaining, so it throws TypeError when evt.destinationCalendar is null or an empty array, whereas the old code used evt.destinationCalendar?.integration and fell through to switching location to Cal Video. Any booking with location set to Google Meet and no destination calendar (the exact scenario this fallback exists for) crashes with 'Cannot read properties of undefined (reading integration)' and the booking fails with a 500 instead of falling back to Cal Video.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/core/EventManager.ts`, the new fallback logic destructures `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [];` and then immediately reads `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` without optional chaining. If `evt.destinationCalendar` is `null`, `undefined`, or an empty array, `mainHostDestinationCalendar` is `undefined` and this will throw a TypeError. The previous code used `evt.destinationCalendar?.integration`, which would not throw and would allow the fallback to Cal Video to execute.
